questions.question: Who informs payroll, and through what process? Does the report go to payroll automatically when the employee submits it, or does HR receive it, check it and then pass it on? AC-03.1.1 says payroll is informed 'when the employee submits', but AC-03.2.1 says HR handles Swiss moves 'on its own'. That suggests HR is in the loop. Is payroll an internal team or an external payroll provider?

What exactly does payroll receive for a move abroad? The ACs only name the new country. Payroll would at least need to know which employee moved. Does payroll also get the full new address and the valid-from date? The Context says the decision 'uses the valid-from date from FEAT-02', and OQ-05 assumes payroll has the new country and the valid-from date. But information.md lists Valid from as needed by HR only, and the trace check says nothing sources payroll receiving even the country. Data minimisation (G-01) makes this choice important.

When must payroll be informed? Right when the report is submitted, only after HR accepts it, or some time before the valid-from date or the payroll run on the 25th? Is there a deadline after which a notification counts as 'missed'?

What happens to the payroll notification in edge cases? Examples: the report is not accepted because the valid-from date is more than three months back (FEAT-02 / OQ-03), the employee corrects or withdraws a report after payroll was informed, or the country is changed from abroad to Switzerland or the other way round. Does payroll get an update or cancellation?

The goal says payroll is 'reliably informed', and P1 says a missed notification puts source tax at risk. What counts as reliable, and how do we test it? Must payroll confirm or acknowledge the notification? Must HR see that payroll was informed? Should anyone be alerted if it fails?

US-03.2 is inferred and says payroll is never involved in Swiss moves. Source-taxed employees who already live in Switzerland are taxed by canton. Does payroll need to know when such an employee changes canton? Also, how do we test 'payroll is not informed'? Does it only mean no notification is sent, or must payroll also have no access to the report? The answer matters if HR and payroll work in the same tool.

Do special territories count as 'abroad'? For example Liechtenstein (which has special tax arrangements with Switzerland), or the enclaves Büsingen (Germany) and Campione d'Italia (Italy). Under the current rule any country other than Switzerland goes to payroll.
Should the employee be told that their report for a move abroad will be passed to payroll?

The example table in AC-03.1.1 is inconsistent. For Germany the 'Country of the new address' result column says 'asked', and for France it says '–', although the two cases are the same. Which result is correct, and what is this column meant to check?

AC-03.1.2 repeats AC-01.2.1 and AC-01.2.2 from FEAT-01 (country always asked, English name). Does it belong to this feature, or is FEAT-01 the only owner? This matters for estimating and for deciding when each story is done.

already_flagged: OQ-04: Whether 'move abroad' means any new country other than Switzerland, and how employees who already live abroad (cross-border staff moving within their country or into Switzerland) are handled
OQ-05: Whether payroll needs further information from the employee to assess source tax, beyond the new country and the valid-from date (payroll not interviewed)
